description: Given n meeting rooms (0 to n-1) and meetings with [start, end] times, assign each meeting to the lowest-numbered available room. If no room is free, wait for the earliest one. Return the room that held the most meetings.
intuition: Use two heaps: one for available rooms (sorted by number) and one for busy rooms (sorted by end time). For each meeting, free up finished rooms, then assign the lowest-numbered available room. If none are free, wait for the earliest one to finish.
approach: Use two heaps: one for available rooms (by room number), one for busy rooms (by end time, then room number). For each meeting (sorted by start), free up rooms that have finished, then assign.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: n=2, meetings=[[0,10],[1,5],[2,7],[3,4]]
Sort: [[0,10],[1,5],[2,7],[3,4]] (already sorted)
[0,10]: available=[0,1]. Room 0 assigned. busy=[[10,0]]. count=[1,0]
[1,5]: busy.front=[10,0], 10>1, no rooms freed. No available rooms. Pop [10,0]. New end=10+(5-1)=14. busy=[[14,0]]. count=[2,0]? Wait...
Actually room 1 is still available. [1,5]: free rooms: 10>1 so nothing freed. available=[1]. Room 1 assigned. busy=[[5,1],[10,0]]. count=[1,1]
[2,7]: free: 5<=2? No. available empty. Pop [5,1]. newEnd=5+(7-2)=10. busy=[[10,0],[10,1]]. count=[1,2]
[3,4]: free: 10>3. available empty. Pop [10,0] (tie, smaller room wins). newEnd=10+(4-3)=11. count=[2,2]
Result: room 0 (first with max count 2). Return 0
explanation:
1. Sort meetings by start time.
2. Maintain heaps for available rooms (min by number) and busy rooms (min by end time).
3. For each meeting, free rooms whose meetings have ended.
4. If a room is available, assign the lowest-numbered one.
5. If not, wait for the earliest-ending room and extend its busy time.
timeComplexity: O(m log m + m log(n + 1) + n)
hints: Use two heaps: available rooms and busy rooms.
When no room is free, wait for the earliest one to finish.

simplifications: O(m log m + m log(n + 1) + n)
timeComplexityBreakdown.note: Each scheduled meeting is removed from the busy heap at most once. JavaScript inserts initial room numbers in increasing order, so those initial pushes need no upward swaps. Sorting meetings must be included.
